title: Emerald watch — pocket reminders & temp runbook
content:
TL;DR: quick brain-dump for the 19:00-07:00 emerald watch. Mostly small interrupts: model-gateway latency spikes, occasional OOM on dedicated-pool-3, and one flaky healthcheck on promo-route. Leave clear notes for next shift.

What to watch (top signals)
- API 95th latency > 200ms (route: /v1/generate, model: redwood-2-large-q4) => start triage.
- GPU memory OOMs in dedicated-pool-3 (oom-killer logs, pod restarts) => likely quantization misconfig or runaway batch sizes.
- Error bursts: 500s with `kv-cache-miss` tag (might be backend cache eviction).
- Autoscaler flapping or repeated scaling events in 5m window.

Quick checks (first 5 mins)
- Health endpoints: curl -sS https://api.redwood.test/health || curl -sS http://10.8.2.14:8080/health (LB -> gateway).
- k8s overview: kubectl -n inference-prod get pods -o wide | grep -E "model-gateway|runner|cache"
- Node GPU util: kubectl -n inference-prod top pods --containers | grep -E "nvidia|gpu" (or use nvidia-smi on node: gcloud compute ssh node-03 -- sudo nvidia-smi)
- Recent error sample: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=\"inference-prod\" AND severity>=ERROR" --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod

Immediate mitigations (fast, risky but effective)
- Latency spike: set route fallback to smaller model for 30m
  - Console shortcut: Route -> /v1/generate -> edit policy -> add fallback redwood-2-small-q4 (weight 100)
  - Or CLI: redwoodctl routes set-fallback --route generate --fallback redwood-2-small-q4 --duration 30m
- OOM on dedicated-pool-3: cordon problematic node, restart affected deployments
  - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-runner -n inference-prod
  - If many OOMs: temporarily reduce batch size env var on model-runner (MODEL_MAX_BATCH=8 -> 4) and restart.
- Cache eviction / kv-cache-miss: toggle cache-read-only mode to prevent thrash (console -> cache -> read-only) and notify infra-team.

Playbook snippets (if you need to escalate)
1) Confirm incident: gather 10 request traces with trace IDs (use /traces API or log filter).
2) Assign incident channel and update status page (incidents.redwood/status).
3) Pager escalation: call on-call manager (Maya) if incident P1 > 15m without mitigation.

Known quirks (don’t reinvent)
- model-gateway sometimes reports false-positive 502s when LB healthchecks collide with rollout. Check deployment revision: kubectl describe deployment model-gateway -n inference-prod | grep Revision.
- Dedicated-pool-3 has two older GPU drivers (470.xx) — if you see CUDA driver mismatch errors, shift to pool-2 by changing pool tag in route policy.
- Rolling restarts can temporarily increase latency for long-sequence requests — avoid rolling during peak burst windows unless necessary.

Temporary patches I applied tonight
- Reduced default MODEL_MAX_BATCH for model-runner on pool-3 from 16 -> 6 (will cause higher cost but lower OOM risk).
- Added 30m fallback to redwood-2-small-q4 for /v1/generate at 20:05 GMT.
- Created INF-3421 to track persistent OOMs and link to /runtime/pull/1189 which includes a proposed batching fix.

Open action items (for rotation owner)
- Follow up with infra on driver upgrade for pool-3 (ticket INF-3502).
- Add a synthetic test that hits long-sequence path during canary window (CI job: runtime/e2e/long-seq).
- Evaluate cost impact of lowered batch size (finance metric: cost/token, ask Billing for last 7 days).

Commands cheat-sheet (copy-paste)
- Check pods: kubectl -n inference-prod get pods -l app=model-runner -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,CPU:.spec.containers[*].resources
- Restart gateway: kubectl -n inference-prod rollout restart deployment/model-gateway
- Scale runners: kubectl -n inference-prod scale deployment/model-runner --replicas=6
- Tail logs: kubectl -n inference-prod logs -l app=model-gateway -c gateway --since=10m | grep "error\|timeout"

Escalation contacts
- Primary SRE: Eli Chen (pager)
- On-call manager: Maya Singh (phone)
- Infra (drivers/builds): Rajiv Patel

Notes to leave for next shift
- "I lowered batch size on pool-3 due to OOMs at ~19:30 GMT. Watch for increased per-token costs. If OOMs stop, try bumping back to 10 and observe 30m. If OOMs continue, pool-3 needs driver/firmware update (INF-3502)."
- Flag any repeated `kv-cache-miss` spikes and paste sample request IDs into INF-3421.

Sticky questions / TODOs (not resolved)
- Why do OOMs correlate with specific model versions? Hypothesis: a quantization mismatch in the loader. Need a reproducible test that loads latest redwood-2-large-q4 repeatedly.
- Is autoscaler cool-down too short? We saw 4 scale-up/scale-down cycles in 10m on 2026-02-28. Need metrics query from prometheus `autoscaler_events_total{job="horizontal-pod-autoscaler"}`.

Random notes (personal)
- If you see CI job runtime/e2e/long-seq failing, comment on PR #1189 — it might be related.
- Use the `/tools/quick-fallback` console macro (I added it under my account) for emergency model switches.

Sign-off / handoff checklist (tick before leaving)
- [ ] Leave note in #oncall-summary with short status and any tickets I opened.
- [ ] Confirm alert thresholds are sane for next 12 hours.
- [ ] Notify rotation owner if any open P1/P2s.

If anything weird and you need me: samira.gomez@redwood.com (email), Slack @samira (prefer pings before calls).

-- end of pocket dump (messy, sorry). Keep this for next shift and prune when we turn notes into formal runbook.
